elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.1 as rendered: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed the greater of ..." and "The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." Existing mutual language retained unchanged.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 21.1: "the greater of (a) all amounts paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000." The temporal anchor matches the playbook's own model language ("twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim"), and "all amounts paid or payable" is at least as broad as fees, so the illusory "Fees"/first-Order-Form basis (USD 12,000) is cured and the USD 1,000,000 floor is present.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.2: "Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill..." — mutual and retained; the direct-damages sentence (restoration, replacement services, notices, incident response) is preserved.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 defines Excluded Claims to include "a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations", and both 21.1 and 21.2 open "Except for Excluded Claims", so confidentiality breach sits outside the cap.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations" is within Excluded Claims, which are excepted from the 21.1 cap.
21.3: "its indemnification obligations" listed as an Excluded Claim, and 21.1 excepts Excluded Claims from the aggregate cap (no sub-cap or super-cap qualifier).
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" within Excluded Claims.
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" within Excluded Claims.
21.3: "...or fraud" within Excluded Claims, excepted from 21.1 and 21.2.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" within Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: 21.3 final sentence: "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section." Present as operative language; the narrow "Fees" definition only shrinks this vendor-side benefit and does not prejudice Customer.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.1: "each Party's total aggregate liability ..."; "The cap is mutual...".

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: 21.1 now keys the cap to "all amounts paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim", replacing the USD 12,000 Implementation-Fee/first-Order-Form basis.
21.3 Excluded Claims include "its indemnification obligations"; 21.1 excepts Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims include "breach of confidentiality... obligations".

reasons: Deviation call is correct: as originally drafted the mutual cap was keyed to "Fees" = the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form only, which is far below 6 months' fees and therefore walk-away/illusory territory notwithstanding the otherwise strong Section 21.

The redline reaches the full preferred checklist: mutual cap, greater-of basis with a USD 1,000,000 floor, mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and uncapped confidentiality/data-protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and other-party IP infringement, plus the payment-obligations carve-out.
Temporal anchor ("twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim") tracks the playbook's own model language, so it is not treated as a weakened variant of "preceding the claim".

Minimal: only the cap basis sentence in 21.1 was edited (dropping the illusory "Fees ... under the first Order Form" basis and adding the floor). 21.2, 21.3 and the favourable direct-damages and mutuality sentences are retained verbatim; no survival tails, procedures, or extra damages categories were added.

Intent preserved: "Fees", "Excluded Claims" and "Order Form" remain defined and used consistently; 21.1 no longer depends on the narrow "Fees" definition but that definition is still operative elsewhere, leaving no dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence. Note for the drafter (rationale only, not a defect): the §1.5 "Fees" definition remains limited to the Implementation Fee, which should be checked against the payment and termination-for-non-payment mechanics under separate rules.
